opening: Lord, meet us gently today and always
body:
Today's readings may initially seem harsh. In Ezekiel 16:1–15, 60, 63, God speaks through Ezekiel about His covenant with Israel. He describes Israel almost as a bride: abandoned at first, then chosen, cared for, loved, and given everything she needed. Yet Israel became unfaithful. God's words are severe because this wasn't simply about breaking rules. It was about betraying a relationship.

But the reading doesn't end with God's anger. God says, **“I will remember the covenant I made with you.”** Despite Israel's unfaithfulness, God remains faithful and promises mercy and restoration. He confronts what happened, but He does not abandon His people.

Then in Matthew 19:3–12, the Pharisees ask Jesus about divorce. Jesus brings them back to God's original intention for marriage: **“The two shall become one flesh... what God has joined together, no human being must separate.”** When they point out that Moses permitted divorce, Jesus explains that this was allowed because of the hardness of people's hearts, but “from the beginning it was not so.”

The connection between the readings is covenant. Ezekiel shows us the pain of covenant broken, while Jesus reminds us what covenant was intended to be. God takes covenant seriously because **He takes love seriously.**

This also connects with Jesus' teaching on forgiveness. Human relationships will experience hurt and failure. Forgiveness doesn't mean pretending the hurt never happened, nor does it require remaining in an abusive or dangerous situation. But God continually calls us away from hardened hearts and toward mercy, faithfulness, and healing.

Perhaps that is the message running through these readings: **God makes covenant. We sometimes fail within it. God confronts what is broken, but He does not stop calling us back. His desire is not simply that we follow better rules, but that our hearts become capable of loving more like His.**
